    def test_should_strip_auth_port_change(self):
        s = requests.Session()
        assert s.should_strip_auth(
            "http://example.com:1234/foo", "https://example.com:4321/bar"
        )

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "old_uri, new_uri",
        (
            ("https://example.com:443/foo", "https://example.com/bar"),
            ("http://example.com:80/foo", "http://example.com/bar"),
            ("https://example.com/foo", "https://example.com:443/bar"),
            ("http://example.com/foo", "http://example.com:80/bar"),
        ),
    )
    def test_should_strip_auth_default_port(self, old_uri, new_uri):
        s = requests.Session()
        assert not s.should_strip_auth(old_uri, new_uri)

    def test_manual_redirect_with_partial_body_read(self, httpbin):
        s = requests.Session()
        r1 = s.get(httpbin("redirect/2"), allow_redirects=False, stream=True)
        assert r1.is_redirect
        rg = s.resolve_redirects(r1, r1.request, stream=True)

        # read only the first eight bytes of the response body,
        # then follow the redirect
        r1.iter_content(8)
        r2 = next(rg)
        assert r2.is_redirect

        # read all of the response via iter_content,
        # then follow the redirect
        for _ in r2.iter_content():
            pass
        r3 = next(rg)
        assert not r3.is_redirect

    def test_prepare_body_position_non_stream(self):
        data = b"the data"
        prep = requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com", data=data).prepare()
        assert prep._body_position is None

    def test_rewind_body(self):
        data = io.BytesIO(b"the data")
        prep = requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com", data=data).prepare()
        assert prep._body_position == 0
        assert prep.body.read() == b"the data"

        # the data has all been read
        assert prep.body.read() == b""

        # rewind it back
        requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)
        assert prep.body.read() == b"the data"

    def test_rewind_partially_read_body(self):
        data = io.BytesIO(b"the data")
        data.read(4)  # read some data
        prep = requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com", data=data).prepare()
        assert prep._body_position == 4
        assert prep.body.read() == b"data"

        # the data has all been read
        assert prep.body.read() == b""

        # rewind it back
        requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)
        assert prep.body.read() == b"data"

    def test_rewind_body_no_seek(self):
        class BadFileObj:
            def __init__(self, data):
                self.data = data

            def tell(self):
                return 0

            def __iter__(self):
                return

        data = BadFileObj("the data")
        prep = requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com", data=data).prepare()
        assert prep._body_position == 0

        with pytest.raises(UnrewindableBodyError) as e:
            requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)

        assert "Unable to rewind request body" in str(e)

    def test_rewind_body_failed_seek(self):
        class BadFileObj:
            def __init__(self, data):
                self.data = data

            def tell(self):
                return 0

            def seek(self, pos, whence=0):
                raise OSError()

            def __iter__(self):
                return

        data = BadFileObj("the data")
        prep = requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com", data=data).prepare()
        assert prep._body_position == 0

        with pytest.raises(UnrewindableBodyError) as e:
            requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)

        assert "error occurred when rewinding request body" in str(e)

    def test_rewind_body_failed_tell(self):
        class BadFileObj:
            def __init__(self, data):
                self.data = data

            def tell(self):
                raise OSError()

            def __iter__(self):
                return

        data = BadFileObj("the data")
        prep = requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com", data=data).prepare()
        assert prep._body_position is not None

        with pytest.raises(UnrewindableBodyError) as e:
            requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)

        assert "Unable to rewind request body" in str(e)

    def _patch_adapter_gzipped_redirect(self, session, url):
        adapter = session.get_adapter(url=url)
        org_build_response = adapter.build_response
        self._patched_response = False

        def build_response(*args, **kwargs):
            resp = org_build_response(*args, **kwargs)

entities.description: The visible test method `test_manual_redirect_with_partial_body_read` performs a streamed request, resolves redirects, partially and fully consumes response bodies with `iter_content`, and asserts redirect status transitions.

The visible test method `test_rewind_partially_read_body` reads four bytes before request preparation, asserts `_body_position == 4`, exhausts the remaining body, rewinds it with `requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)`, and asserts `b"data"` can be read again.

The visible test method `test_rewind_body` prepares a request from `io.BytesIO`, asserts an initial body position of `0`, reads the body to exhaustion, calls `requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)`, and asserts the original bytes can be read again.

`REQUESTS.UTILS.REWIND_BODY` refers to the external callable `requests.utils.rewind_body`, which is used with `prep` to rewind the body of a prepared request. The provided material shows only its invocation and does not include the callable’s definition or implementation details.

The visible test method `test_rewind_body_no_seek` defines a file-like object without `seek`, prepares it as request data, and asserts that `requests.utils.rewind_body(prep)` raises `UnrewindableBodyError` containing `Unable to rewind request body`.

Defines the test method `test_HTTP_307_ALLOW_REDIRECT_POST_WITH_SEEKABLE`; posts an `io.BytesIO` body through a 307 redirect and asserts status 200, redirect history status 307, redirect state, and decoded response data.
The attribute call `s.resolve_redirects(resp, prep_req)` is explicitly referenced; the receiver's concrete runtime class is not proven by this chunk.

The visible test method `test_rewind_body_failed_seek` defines a file-like object whose `seek` raises `OSError`, then asserts that rewinding raises `UnrewindableBodyError` containing `error occurred when rewinding request body`.
`seek` is explicitly retrieved from `prepared_request.body` and then called through `body_seek(...)` in `rewind_body`; the receiver's concrete implementation is not visible.

Defined here as `def test_redirect_rfc1808_to_non_ascii_location()`. It creates a redirect handler, follows a redirect, and asserts the final status, history, percent-encoded non-ASCII path, and second request line.

`REWIND_BODY` refers to the `rewind_body` utility, which is imported from `.utils`. It is used to rewind a consumed file-like request body when the `rewindable` option is enabled. Its implementation is not visible in the provided code, and no direct usage appears in the referenced chunk beyond the import.

The visible test method `test_rewind_body_failed_tell` defines a file-like object whose `tell` raises `OSError`, asserts `_body_position is not None`, and asserts that rewinding raises `UnrewindableBodyError` containing `Unable to rewind request body`.
`UnrewindableBodyError` is defined here as a subclass of `RequestException` and represents failure while rewinding a request body.

Defined here as `def test_fragment_update_on_redirect()`. Its documentation claims redirect fragments should be retained only when a later Location lacks a new fragment; the visible setup uses a response handler that sends two 302 responses followed by a 200 response.
References the unresolved receiver operation `r.request.body.seek(self._thread_local.pos)` in `handle_401` when a saved body position exists; the runtime type of `r.body` is not established.

The test function `test_requests_in_history_are_not_overridden` is defined here. It performs `requests.get(httpbin("redirect/3"))` and asserts response history URLs equal the corresponding request URLs.

Defined here as the nested `def redirect_resp_handler(sock)`. It consumes an initial request, sends a 301 response with a `Location` containing `path`, records a second request in `redirect_request`, and sends a 200 response.

`test_digestauth_401_count_reset_on_redirect()` is defined here and documents a digest-authentication redirect scenario involving a successful authentication followed by a 302 redirect to another digest prompt; the visible chunk ends while defining response data, before any executable assertion or request call is shown.

The test function `test_requests_are_updated_each_time` is defined here; it sends a prepared POST request through `RedirectSession`, follows redirects, and asserts recorded redirect requests use `GET`.
